description: Ordering-rule vector table for the published catalogue contract (unit 1d-a). This document is NOT a snapshot and NOT a query result: it is a hand-authored, clearly-labelled table of adversarial raw model IDs and their literal expected natural order. Every 'expected' array is literal, never computed by an implementation. It exists so the provider-display-order + natural-raw-ID-order rule is pinned before any runtime extraction.
ordering_rule: Provider precedence is the index in provider_order (never alphabetic key order); within a provider, raw IDs compare by the natural comparator: only maximal ASCII [0-9]+ runs are digit runs, compared by ORIGINAL digit count then lexical ASCII digits (no integer/float conversion, no leading-zero stripping); text segments compare case-sensitively by Unicode code point (no case folding, locale collation, Unicode normalization or UTF-16 code-unit comparison); digit-run tokens precede text tokens; on a strict prefix the shorter token sequence sorts first; literal raw IDs are never rewritten.

cases.why: Natural order keeps the ORIGINAL digit count, then lexical ASCII digits: item1/item2 (1 digit) < item02/item10 (2 digits, 02 < 10) < item000 (3 digits). Numeric-value normalization would move item000 (== 0) to the front; leading zeroes are never stripped.

Two 64-digit runs differing only in the final digit, supplied in REVERSE correct order: length is equal so the comparison is lexical on the ASCII digits and ...91 precedes ...92. Float conversion of both runs yields the SAME double, so a float-based key collides and leaves the reversed input untouched.
Adjacent run lengths: a 64-digit run precedes a 65-digit run whatever their numeric values, because the original digit count is compared first.

Boundary strings '2', '10', 'a', superscript two and Arabic-Indic one: only maximal ASCII [0-9]+ runs are digit runs ('2' len 1, '10' len 2), digit runs precede text tokens, and the text tokens compare by code point (a U+0061 < superscript-two U+00B2 < Arabic-Indic-one U+0661). str.isdigit()/\d/Number() classify the two non-ASCII characters as numeric and are NOT the contract.

Code-point order: 'vendor/B' < 'vendor/a' proves no case folding; 'vendor/Ａ' (U+FF21, BMP) precedes 'vendor/😀' (U+1F600, astral) even though native UTF-16 code-unit order reverses them (surrogate D83D < FF21).
Equal token prefix then trailing text: the empty boundary text token of 'vendor/item1' is preserved and the shorter sequence sorts first, then '-' (U+002D) < 'a' (U+0061).
Leading-zero numeric-value ties: 1, 01 and 001 all have numeric value 1, but the runs are compared by original digit count (1 < 2 < 3) with the zeroes retained.
